entries.title: Bears' grades are in. How did they do against the Saints?
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/22/bears-saints-halftime-score-16-10-caleb-williams-tyler-shough-touchdowns-field-goal-nfl-soldier-field-sunday" target="_blank" >Bears’ 21-13 win against the Saints</a> was anything but pretty, though the defense put on a show with six sacks and a couple of takeaways.</p><p>Where do the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> go from here? Back into the lab offensively, and then to Detroit for a Thanksgiving game.</p><p>Sunday could have gone a lot better at Soldier Field, but fans didn't leave too unhappy about the team's 8-2 record.</p><p>Let's get to the grades:</p><h3><b>QUARTERBACK — C</b></h3><p>It wouldn’t be fair to consider Caleb Williams’ 100.1 passer rating and say he had a bad game against the Saints. On the other hand, it’s hard to see that 100.1 — higher than Williams’ season average, by the way — and think too highly of it. Tight end Colston Loveland did all the hard work on one of Williams’ touchdown passes, and the other was a shovel pass to running back D’Andre Swift that the QB simply had to not screw up. Williams threw a 40-yard dime to Zavion Thomas that was his biggest highlight; even better, he scrambled for a couple of first downs at full speed, a sign that his hamstring injury is completely behind him. Otherwise, he held the ball a bit too long and failed to convert on a bunch of third and fourth downs. His interception, tipped at the line by the Saints’ Carl Granderson and hauled in by Danny Stutsman, was just rotten luck.</p><h3><b>RUNNING BACKS — C</b></h3><p>Coach Ben Johnson wasn’t thrilled with D’Andre Swift’s 3.9 yards per carry, and that was before Swift’s fourth-quarter fumble gave the Saints life — hello, doghouse. The crowd was psyched to see Kyle Monangai run out there after a five-game injury absence, but he made no impact of note on his eight carries. Hey, how ’bout that 19-yard rush by practice-squadder Salvon Ahmed! The Bears aimed to dominate this game on the ground but didn’t come close to doing so.</p><h3><b>RECEIVERS — B</b></h3><p>After a loss, Rome Odunze and Luther Burden’s combined seven catches for 69 yards might be a glaring disappointment. Instead, they get to move on quietly enough while we throw bouquets at third-round rookie Thomas, a blazer whose aforementioned 40-yard catch was merely his third-best play of the game. He got into top gear on a 30-yard reverse, exciting to see. And on a fourth-quarter third down, he moved the chains with an extremely difficult 16-yard catch made while sliding on his stomach. Loveland made his best highlight play since the end of last year’s win in Cincinnati, hurdling Saints safety Julian Blackmon en route to the end zone.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Colston Loveland hurdle and TD!<br><br>NOvsCHI on FOX/FOX One<br>Stream on <a href="https://x.com/NFLPlus?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@NFLPlus</a> <a href="https://t.co/F1Ivvb3Pas">pic.twitter.com/F1Ivvb3Pas</a></p>— NFL (@NFL) <a href="https://x.com/NFL/status/2124579302243270946?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 22, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>DEFENSIVE LINE — A</b></h3><p>Not to put the cart ahead of the horse, but this Jeffery Simmons kid has a chance to make something of himself in this league. Simmons — who has “Bears great” written all over him — threw three more sacks onto his pile of thoroughly impressive work in three games since being traded here. Three cheers for his sack celebration, which doesn’t involve jumping. Simmons overpowered guard David Edwards so easily on the way to one sack, Edwards might as well have been back in his days as Downers Grove North’s quarterback. Simmons and Montez Sweat each abused undrafted rookie tackle Mason Murphy on the way to sacks, Sweat’s coming in the end zone for a safety that made it 21-10. What did Murphy ever do to anyone to deserve those one-on-one assignments?</p><h3><b>SECONDARY — A-MINUS</b></h3><p>The Bears have to be feeling good about the first-round selection of safety Dillon Thieneman after his interception of Tyler Shough and his textbook tackle of Barion Brown on a reverse. Clark Phillips forced a CJ Donaldson fumble with a hit over the middle and hung with it after being picked up on a blitz to record first career sack. Cam Lewis had a third-down sack on a blitz off the edge. Lewis whiffed on a tackle attempt that allowed Travis Etienne to rumble for a 46-yard gain, but cornerback Jaylon Johnson took a perfect angle from across the field and ran down Etienne before the running back could reach the end zone; it nearly saved seven points, but the Saints eventually scored on fourth-and-goal.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/22/bears-saints-halftime-score-16-10-caleb-williams-tyler-shough-touchdowns-field-goal-nfl-soldier-field-sunday" target="_blank" >Bears, QB Caleb Williams good enough to topple lowly Saints</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Man fatally shot in Roseland
entries.summary: <p>A man was shot and killed in Roseland Sunday afternoon, police said.</p><p>The man, 28, was on the street in the 0-100 block of West 111th Street when someone fired shots, striking him in the chest, according to Chicago police.</p><p>He was taken to Roseland Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.</p><p>No one is in custody ,and detectives are investigating.</p>

As We Fix Our Nation’s Broken Heart” tour in 2024, Steve Wonder’s latest shows convey an urgent call for spreading love and fostering unity.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Bill Smith/United Center</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>A few songs later, there was another gut punch: During “Pastime Paradise,” the video screen displayed images of 14-year-old Chicagoan <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/arts-and-culture/2026/06/07/emmett-till-blanc-gallery-black-boyhood-exhibit-civil-rights-art" target="_blank" ><u>Emmett Till</u></a>, whose racially motivated murder in 1955 helped spur the Civil Rights Movement.</p><p>Those two moments underscored the intentionality of Wonder’s “‘Songs in the Key of Life’ 50th Anniversary Tour,” celebrating his seminal 1976 album. At 76, the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer could rest on his laurels by retiring or choosing to deliver a simpler presentation of his hits. But, much like his “Sing Your Song! As We Fix Our Nation’s Broken Heart” <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/music/2024/11/03/stevie-wonder-review-united-center-chicago-sing-your-song-tour-set-list" target="_blank" ><u>tour in 2024</u></a>, his latest shows convey an urgent call for spreading love and fostering unity.</p><p>“The universe is in alignment, but we are not,” said Wonder, who was backed by a stellar, approximately 30-piece band. “And we need to work that out.”</p><p>Wonder struck a perfect balance of seriousness and levity, as well as joy and heartache during the three-hour show. He set that intention when he appeared onstage, asking the audience to meditate on the “beauty” of hope, pain and sorrow. From there, he performed “Songs in the Key of Life” in its entirety, beginning with “Love’s in Need of Love Today,” which earned a standing ovation.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div Center</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Wonder, visibly moved, said he was emotional because he had “special friends in the audience.” He didn’t name them, but there were celebrities in the building, including Chance the Rapper, who posted a video clip from the show on his Instagram Stories. “I have tears in my eyes,” he wrote.</p><p>Wonder showed off a couple of snazzy outfits, trading in a leopard-print jacket for a glittery gold suit with matching sunglasses after a 15-minute intermission. Though a bit raspy at times, he was otherwise in good voice, eliciting cheers whenever he slid into his upper register. And his harmonica solos were as vibrant as ever.</p><p>He kept the attendees entertained between telling jokes (Garrett Popcorn was one topic of discussion), leading call-and-response chants and playing off his band, which included some of his children (daughter Aisha Morris, of “Isn’t She Lovely” fame was present). The group also featured original “Songs in the Key of Life” bassist Nathan Watts and keyboardist Greg Phillinganes, who served as music director of the show.</p><p>The musicians especially showed off their chops on the frenzied “Contusion,” which generated a huge smile of satisfaction from Wonder, and the leisurely “Easy Goin’ Evening (My Mama’s Call).” Other crowd-pleasers included “Sir Duke,” “Knocks Me Off My Feet” and a particularly sentimental version of “Joy Inside My Tears.”</p><p>While Wonder didn’t play any of the album outtakes that he recently released on “Songs in the Key of Life - The EP,” he did perform some bonus hits, including “My Cherie Amour,” “Superstition” and John Lennon’s “Imagine.” He also paid homage to Chicago, riffing about the city during a surprise rendition of “Billie Jean” and a blues number he played on the harpejji stringed instrument.</p><p> Wonder achieved his quest for unity, as his show brought together people of all ages and ethnic backgrounds. Among them was Emma Rubin, 28, of Seattle. She said she had heard some tracks from “Songs in the Key of LIfe” growing up but decided to listen to the album in its entirety five years ago.</p><p>“I kept going back to it,” said Rubin, who has family in Skokie.<b> </b>“I think the songs just carry a lot of emotion to them and take you to a lot of different places.”</p><p>South Side native Amahdy Bradley, 54, said the album was an important representation of the Black experience.</p><p>“Stevie is the actual Black movement to me, and ‘Songs in the Key of Life’ takes you to all the things that we went through as a people, as well as accepting the beauty that we see in the world,” he said. </p><p>Fifty years later, Wonder is still unafraid to speak his mind, taking “the leaders on this earth” to task before performing “Saturn,” a yearning for escapism from the condition of the world.</p><p>“You’ve been given the opportunity by the people to make the world a better place,” he said. “And when you don’t do that, you become what I call a f--- up. But you can do better, and you need to handle your business.”</p><p>For everyone else, he had a simple command:<b> </b>“Love somebody.”</p><p>“And if your heart is big enough, love every somebody.”</p><h2>Set list for Stevie Wonder at United Center Nov. 21, 2026</h2><p>Love's in Need of Love Today<br>Have a Talk With God<br>Village Ghetto Land<br>Contusion<br>Sir Duke<br>I Wish<br>Knocks Me Off My Feet<br>My Cherie Amour<br>Billie Jean<br>Pastime Paradise<br>Summer Soft<br>Ordinary Pain<br>Saturn<br>Ebony Eyes</p><p><i>-Set Break-</i></p><p>Isn't She Lovely<br>Joy Inside My Tears<br>Black Man<br>All Day Sucker<br>Easy Goin' Evening (My Mama's Call)<br>Ngiculela - Es Una Historia - I Am Singing<br>Blues Jam<br>If It's Magic<br>As<br>Happy Birthday<br>Another Star<br>Imagine<br>Superstition</p>
